questions.text:
A commercially sold conc. HCl is $35 \% \mathrm{HCl}$ by mass. If the density of this commercial acid is 1.46 g/mL, the molarity of this solution is :
(Atomic mass : $\mathrm{Cl}=35.5 \mathrm{amu}, \mathrm{H}=1 \mathrm{amu}$ )

options.D:
18.2 M

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. Let total volume $=1000 \mathrm{~mL}=1 \mathrm{~L}$
total mass of solution $=1460 \mathrm{~g}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { mass of } \mathrm{HCl}=\frac{35}{100} \times 1460 \\
\text { moles of } \mathrm{HCl}=\frac{35 \times 1460}{100 \times 36.5} \\
\text { So molarity }=\frac{35 \times 1460}{100 \times 36.5}=14 \mathrm{M}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
An evacuated glass vessel weighs 40.0 g when empty, 135.0 g when filled with a liquid of density $0.95 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}$ and 40.5 g when filled with an ideal gas at 0.82 atm at 250 K . The molar mass of the gas in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is :
(Given : $\mathrm{R}=0.082 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ )

options.D:
125

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. Mass of liquid $=135-40=95 \mathrm{~g}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { Volume of liquid }=\frac{\text { mass }}{\text { density }}=\frac{95}{.95} \mathrm{~mL} \\
=100 \mathrm{~mL}=0.1 \mathrm{~L} \\
\text { mass of ideal gas }=40.5-40 \mathrm{~g}=0.5 \mathrm{~g} \\
\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT} \\
0.82 \times 0.1=\left(\frac{0.5}{\mathrm{M}}\right) \times 0.082 \times 250
\end{array}$$

steps:
Mass of liquid $=135-40=95 \mathrm{~g}$
$$\begin{array}{l}

=100 \mathrm{~mL}=0.1 \mathrm{~L} \\
\text { mass of ideal gas }=40.5-40 \mathrm{~g}=0.5 \mathrm{~g} \\
\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT} \\

\end{array}$$

questions.text: If the radius of the $3^{\text {rd }}$ Bohr's orbit of hydrogen atom is $\mathrm{r}_{3}$ and the radius of $4{ }^{\text {th }}$ Bohr's orbit is $\mathrm{r}_{4}$. Then :

options.D:
$\mathrm{r}_{4}=\frac{4}{3} \mathrm{r}_{3}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $\mathrm{r}=0.529 \times \frac{\mathrm{n}^{2}}{\mathrm{z}} \AA$

\mathrm{r}_{3}=0.529 \times \frac{3^{2}}{1} \\
\mathrm{r}_{4}=0.529 \times \frac{4^{2}}{1} \\
\frac{\mathrm{r}_{4}}{\mathrm{r}_{3}}=\frac{4^{2}}{3^{2}}=\frac{16}{9} \\
\mathrm{r}_{4}=\frac{16 \mathrm{r}_{3}}{9}
\end{array}$$

A B C D
